comments.text:
The real truth..Animal agriculture is a major driver of global water scarcity and drought. It accounts for roughly one-third of the world's freshwater consumption. The vast majority of this water—up to 98%—is used to irrigate water-intensive feed crops like corn and soy, making meat and dairy production extremely inefficient during dry periods.The impact of animal agriculture on water supplies can be broken down into three major areas:Feed Crop Irrigation: The water required to grow feed accounts for most of the industry's footprint. For instance, producing just one pound of beef takes approximately 1,800 gallons of water, much of which is drawn from depleting aquifers like the Ogallala in the American West.Direct Consumption: Livestock requires billions of gallons of drinking water and is heavily used to clean factory farms, lorries, and slaughterhouses.Water Pollution: Runoff from massive feedlots and factory farms introduces manure, antibiotics, and fertilizers into the water table, drastically reducing the amount of safe, usable freshwater available for communities.
If people would cut their consumption of animals by 50%, we could have all the water we needed. The people have “gotta have that meat“
